differentiators.heading: Four decades of continuity
differentiators.text: The firm was established in 1984. Our founding partners have been in practice since the mid-1980s. That continuity means we have seen Indian business through multiple regulatory regimes, economic cycles, and structural shifts — and our advice is informed by that depth.

differentiators.heading: Senior attention, not junior throughput
differentiators.text: We are a partner-led firm. The partner assigned to your engagement is accountable for the quality of the advice and the outcome of the matter. We do not operate on a model where a senior takes the brief, and a junior delivers the work without oversight.

differentiators.heading: Breadth that holds together
differentiators.text: Most CA firms specialise in one or two areas. ARSK handles statutory audit, direct and indirect tax, international taxation, corporate law, FEMA, NCLT matters, valuations, and M&A support — with named specialists for each. When your matters intersect, we manage that intersection.

differentiators.heading: Genuine India expertise
differentiators.text: We are an Indian firm, advising on Indian law, for clients operating in India. We understand the Indian regulatory personality — the practical realities of assessment proceedings, the texture of SEBI and RBI interactions, the dynamics of appellate litigation. That is not a secondary capability; it is our primary one.

differentiators.heading: Two cities, one firm
differentiators.text: Our Kolkata headquarters and Mumbai branch operate as one firm, not as franchises. Clients with interests in both cities — or with counterparties in either — get consistent advice and coordinated service across regional borders.

differentiators.heading: Candid Objectivity
differentiators.text: We will be clear about what can be achieved, candid about what cannot, and measured in assessing potential outcomes. In tax disputes, regulatory matters and commercial negotiations, our role is to provide preparation, representation and professional judgement—not promises regarding outcomes that remain outside anyone's control.
